name: Playground Global
identity_check: Confirmed as Playground Global, the Palo Alto deep-tech venture firm founded in 2015 (Peter Barrett and Bruce Leak are named co-founders; 2015 press calls it Andy Rubin's venture). playground.global now 301-redirects to www.playground.vc; the site calls the firm 'Playground', its footer reads 'Playground Global', and it gives HQ as 380 Portage Ave, Palo Alto, with $1.7B AUM. SEC EDGAR lists Playground Global, LLC and the Playground Ventures I-IV, Affiliates and Omega fund entities at the same 380 Portage Avenue address. Started in 2015 as a hardware incubator/studio and now a deep-tech VC. Not to be confused with unrelated companies that use the 'Playground' name (e.g. a Sofia-based Playground Energy seen in search results).

'about $242 million in funding as part of a projected $300 million fundraise' across Playground Global and Playground Ventures (TechCrunch, 2017-06-30)
conflicts.chosen: Fund I = $300M (Playground Ventures, L.P.); the $48M Playground Global, LLC raise kept as its own entry
conflicts.reason: The press treats the 2015 money as one ~$300M raise spanning the Playground Global, LLC and Playground Ventures, L.P. filings, so the $48M is probably inside the $300M; do not add the two. The Form D documents on sec.gov refused the declared User-Agent, so the split could not be checked.

open_items: No application form or pitch URL: the site offers only a general 'Let's talk' mailto link (not recorded) and /contact returns 404; accepts_cold_inbound left 'unknown'.

Nothing found on investing in Indian founders or on requiring a US entity. The portfolio includes Australian companies (Syenta, Element Zero) and Milan-based Sizable Energy, so a US entity is evidently not always required at investment, but no policy is stated.

portfolio_count_reported not stated anywhere: the portfolio page lists 46 companies as 'some of the companies' Playground has backed. The About page gives '$1.7 billion in assets under management' (no schema field for AUM).

SEC EDGAR: data.sec.gov and the full-text search accepted the declared User-Agent, but www.sec.gov/Archives refused it, so Form D amounts were not read. Entities found at 380 Portage Ave: Playground Global, LLC (Form D 2015-04-06, D/A 2016-02-01, D 2017-01-11); Playground Ventures, L.P. (2015-04-06); Playground Ventures II (2016-11-22); Affiliates II (2017-06-30); Playground Ventures III (2022-02-10); Affiliates III (2022-06-14); Playground Ventures IV and Affiliates IV (2024-12-19, D/A 2026-07-02); Playground Omega, L.P. (2025-05-28, D/A 2025-07-08); Playground Omega 2, L.P. (2025-07-08). Purpose and size of the Omega vehicles (possibly SPVs/opportunity funds) unknown.

Fund II final close, exact Fund I close date and the Affiliates II final amount were not found ($15M is the 2017 Form D offering amount reported by TechCrunch, none sold at the time). Axios (Yoler interview, Fund IV story) and FinSMEs returned 403.

No robotics / automation / manufacturing round with Playground was found in the last 24 months; the most recent robotics rounds recorded are Boxbot (2023) and Agility Robotics (2022). Agility is going public via a SPAC with Churchill Capital Corp XI (S-4 effective 2026-10-13, ~$200M PIPE led by Foxconn); Agility names Playground Global as an existing investor, but no Playground participation in the PIPE is stated, so it is not recorded as a round. Robust.AI's press releases contain no funding round.

Rounds not recorded: Unreasonable Labs ~$13.5M (Feb/Mar 2026, reportedly led by Playground) seen only in search-result text and database listings; GigaCrop (Playground post 2025-03-11 says Playground is investing $4.5M; round size, stage and co-investors not stated); Ideon Series A (2022); Agility's 2018 $8M Series A and 2020 $20M round (search hints only). A MarketScreener snippet giving Sizable Energy's round as €6.89M led by Possible Ventures was not fetched or verified.

BusinessWire releases (Syenta, Sizable Energy, Alva Energy, Agility 2022) and Reuters returned 403 or were blocked; rounds rely on company pages and trade press instead. Founding years not stated for most portfolio companies; HQ not stated for XRlabs and Vertical Semiconductor; XRlabs website not given.

Partners: Clinton Lazzari's LinkedIn link on the site goes through a LinkedIn authwall, so no profile URL is recorded. Matt Hershenson is listed as Venture Partner but his bio calls him a Founding Partner. Focus sectors are mapped from each profile's 'Investment Focus' tags (Automation, Robotics, Next-Gen Compute, Infrastructure, Energy Transition, Life Sciences) and bio text; Jory Bell's industrial tag reflects his Relativity Space and Velo3D investments. Andy Rubin, a 2015 co-founder per press, does not appear on the current People page.
